hints: Focus on what each reagent does, $	ext{NaBH}_4$ reduces only aldehydes and ketones to alcohols, while hot acidified $	ext{K}_2	ext{Cr}_2	ext{O}_7$ oxidises alcohols and aldehydes fully.
Notice the reduction product is glycerol, $	ext{HOCH}_2	ext{CH(OH)CH}_2	ext{OH}$, so X must already have that 3-carbon skeleton with one carbonyl that becomes an alcohol.
Check which candidates can be oxidised up to $	ext{HO}_2	ext{CCOCO}_2	ext{H}$ with two $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ ends and a central ketone, and which one cannot.
walkthrough:
**Decode the two reactions**

Think like a detective. $	ext{NaBH}_4$ is a gentle reducing agent. It turns aldehydes into primary alcohols and ketones into secondary alcohols, but it leaves carboxylic acids alone.

Hot acidified $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ is a powerful oxidiser. It turns primary alcohols and aldehydes into carboxylic acids, and secondary alcohols into ketones.

**Use the reduction to glycerol**

The reduction product is:
$$\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{OH}$$
This is glycerol with formula $\text{C}_3\text{H}_8\text{O}_3$. Since X is $\text{C}_3\text{H}_6\text{O}_3$, X has two fewer H atoms, exactly what you expect if one $\text{C-OH}$ was a $\text{C=O}$.

So X must contain an aldehyde or ketone that $	ext{NaBH}_4$ can reduce.

**Test structures 2 and 3**

Structure 2 is $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH(OH)CHO}$, glyceraldehyde. Reduction of the $\text{CHO}$ gives glycerol. Oxidation: $\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ to $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$, $\text{CH(OH)}$ to $\text{CO}$, $\text{CHO}$ to $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$:
$$\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH(OH)CHO} \rightarrow \text{HO}_2\text{CCOCO}_2\text{H}$$
This fits perfectly.

Structure 3 is $\text{HOCH}_2\text{COCH}_2\text{OH}$, dihydroxyacetone. Reduction of the central ketone gives glycerol. Oxidation of both $\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ ends gives:
$$\text{HOCH}_2\text{COCH}_2\text{OH} \rightarrow \text{HO}_2\text{CCOCO}_2\text{H}$$
This also fits perfectly.

**Reject structure 1**

Structure 1 is $\text{HOCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$, 3-hydroxypropanoic acid. $\text{NaBH}_4$ will not reduce the $\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ group, so you cannot get glycerol.

Its oxidation would give $\text{HO}_2\text{CCH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{H}$, propanedioic acid, not the keto-diacid observed.

Conclusion: only 2 and 3 are possible.

options.A: Incorrect because it includes 1 with 2 and 3. Structure 1 contains a carboxylic acid which $	ext{NaBH}_4$ cannot reduce, so it can never form glycerol, and its oxidation gives a different diacid.
options.B: Incorrect because it includes 1. Although 2 is correct, 1 fails both tests: no reducible aldehyde or ketone for $	ext{NaBH}_4$, and wrong oxidation product.
options.C: Correct because both 2 and 3 work. Both have formula $	ext{C}_3	ext{H}_6	ext{O}_3$, both reduce at the carbonyl to glycerol with $	ext{NaBH}_4$, and both oxidise fully to $	ext{HO}_2	ext{CCOCO}_2	ext{H}$ with hot acidified dichromate.
options.D: Incorrect because it is incomplete. Structure 3 alone is indeed possible, dihydroxyacetone reduces to glycerol and oxidises correctly, but it misses that structure 2, glyceraldehyde, is equally possible.
